correctness.rationale: The exact sampling law gives mean-zero sign and variance 1/q, closing the diagonal covariance at T_q. Strictly positive Perron overlap for any nonzero initial error makes lambda_max(T_q) the exact mean-square exponential factor and handles critical nondecay. The explicitly factored det(I-T_q) and diagonal principal minor prove if-and-only-if stability for every alpha>0. The exact one-step matrix gives alpha_one and rational witness. Strict positivity of the Perron eigenvalue second derivative proves unique optimum in (1,2), and the rescaled delta=1-c expansion and stationary equation give stated constants. The embedded stdlib checker passed 1,220 exact/numerical diagnostic tests; numerical tests are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The original averaged-Kaczmarz paper (2020, §§1,3--5 and appendix) bounds one-step squared error and optimizes a guaranteed rate, but does not derive an exact two-row long-time moment spectral radius, sharp beyond-one-step relaxation boundary, or a provably transiently amplifying convergent interval. The broader sketch-and-project and sparse averaging texts concern bound optimization or different updates; classical exact MSE pertains to one-row projection. Indexed close results concern different state maps. A plausible equivalent unindexed computation remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by a published parallel Kaczmarz averaging solver whose prescribed relaxations optimize one-step rate bounds. The exact sharp long-horizon stability frontier identifies a nonempty, mathematically counterintuitive zone of transient expected-error growth with eventual geometric convergence, and the exact optimizer quantifies an algorithmically natural tuning limit. The finite-dimensional family is minimal for row correlation and has a robust full interval, not a single arbitrary parameter example.
